title: Desmos Basics: Sliders for Unknown Constants

beats.say: When an equation contains an unknown constant, Desmos offers a slider for it. You drag the slider, and the graph changes while you watch.

card.text: A slider makes a constant adjustable

beats.say: To add a slider yourself, type an equation that uses a new letter, such as k. Desmos creates the slider automatically, and you can click its ends to change its range.

card.text: New letter in an equation = new slider

beats.say: We'll work through three examples, from an easy one to a hard one, and you'll see every key press.
Easy example. The line y equals k x plus one passes through the point two comma seven. What's the value of k?
We'll graph the line with a slider for k, plot the point, and slide k until the line passes through the point.
Type y equals k x plus one. Desmos notices the new letter k and creates a slider for it.
Now type the point, two comma seven, as an ordered pair. It appears on the graph as a dot, and the line doesn't pass through it yet.
Drag the slider upward. The line gets steeper, and when k reaches three, the line passes exactly through the point.
So k equals three. We can check with algebra: three times two plus one is seven, which is the y value of the point.
Medium example. For the equation y equals x squared plus k x plus nine, find the positive value of k for which the parabola touches the x axis at exactly one point.
A parabola that just touches the x axis has exactly one solution. We'll use a slider to find when that happens.
Type y equals x, the caret key and a two, the right arrow, then plus k x plus nine. Desmos creates a slider for k.
Now slide k downward from ten. At first, the parabola crosses the x axis twice. Watch for the moment it only touches the axis.
At k equals six, the parabola touches the x axis at a single point. Below six, it floats above the axis and has no solutions at all.
Hard example. For the equation two x squared plus k x plus eight equals zero, what positive value of k gives exactly one real solution?
Exactly one real solution means the parabola y equals two x squared plus k x plus eight touches the x axis once. We graph it with a slider.
Type y equals two x, the caret key and a two, the right arrow, then plus k x plus eight.
Slide k downward from twelve. The parabola moves from crossing the axis twice, to touching it once, to missing it entirely.
The touch happens at k equals eight. We can confirm with the discriminant: k squared minus four times two times eight is k squared minus sixty-four, which is zero when k is eight.
To recap. Type an equation with a new letter, and Desmos adds a slider for it automatically.
beats.item: A new letter creates a slider

beats.say: Slide until the graph does what the question describes, such as passing through a point, or touching the x axis once.
beats.item: Slide until the graph matches the question

beats.say: If you have time, confirm with the discriminant or with algebra. In the next video, we solve any equation by graphing.
beats.item: Confirm with algebra if time allows
